# Twig

> **Status: ongoing project, early stage.** Its main purpose is to demonstrate *how*
> the goal below could be achieved — validating the approach and the toolchain, not
> delivering finished firmware.

## Target

Twig is an attempt to run **Mingle/Runtime** directly on a microcontroller:
take a transpiled `.model` file (the same JSON model that `stick.jar` runs on a full
JVM) and execute it on an **FreeRTOS**, using only C++.

Only a subset of Mingle/Runtime features and drivers are supported.

## Using the scripts

All scripts live at the project root or under `tools/`, and expect ESP-IDF to be
installed and exported (`$IDF_PATH`).

- **`./run.sh <model.model> [--seconds N] [--skip-check]`**
  The single entry point: runs all host unit-test suites, then checks, builds and boots
  the given `.model` under QEMU. Fails fast if any test suite fails.

- **`tools/check_model.sh <model.model>`**
  Runs only the compatibility check — reports whether the model can run on twig-oop at
  all, without building anything.

- **`tools/build_model.sh <model.model> [--qemu] [--seconds N] [--skip-check]`**
  Checks compatibility, selects only the drivers the model needs, embeds the model into
  the firmware, and builds it. Add `--qemu` to also boot the result under QEMU.

- **`tools/run_model.sh <model.model> [--seconds N] [--skip-check]`**
  Shortcut for `build_model.sh --qemu` — the quickest dev loop from `.model` file to a
  booted, running image in QEMU.

- **`./run_qemu.sh [seconds]`**
  Lower-level: builds the current `idf.py` project as-is and boots it under QEMU,
  printing the serial console for the given duration. Used internally by the scripts
  above; useful on its own when iterating on firmware code without changing the
  embedded model.

For a real board instead of QEMU, build with `tools/build_model.sh <model.model>` and
flash manually with `idf.py -p <PORT> flash monitor` — there is no fleet/multi-target
deploy story yet, by design, given this is still a single-board PoC.
